title: TST-1 — Tag Semantic Token Delivery
summary: add a separate Tag semantic family whose rendered occurrence is followed by its ordered document associations
content_html:
TST-1 — Tag Semantic Token Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as TST-1, a standalone delivery beneath Semantic Tokens. It is not active and does not authorize implementation.

The delivery adds Tag as a second Semantic Tokens family after the Tag Registry acquired canonical document associations. It keeps Tag separate from Catalogue: a Work, Series, or Moment resolves to one concrete catalogue destination, while a Tag resolves to its complete ordered set of associated documents.

Complete Outcome

In Manage Source, an author selects meaningful text, chooses Add tag token, searches canonical Tags and aliases, and selects one exact canonical tag_id. The built document retains the authored text and follows it with the Tag's current associated document links:

nerve ([Nerve], [Neural pathways])

The source records stable Tag identity rather than copying document URLs. A normal rebuild resolves the current ordered doc_url[] projection, emits the bounded parenthesised link group, and records one Tag-token occurrence in the scope usage index. The public document contains ordinary resolved links and no Tag Registry, target lookup, or client-side semantic resolver.

Fixed Product Direction

Separate Family And Action

  • Tag is a separate Semantic Tokens family with its own Add tag token action, discovery modal, parser contribution, and Info view.
  • Tag is not added to Add catalogue token search. Catalogue continues to combine only Work, Series, and Moment.
  • The Tag family reuses the generic source selection, guarded range mutation, modal lifecycle, token registry, target lookup, build projection, usage index, report, and Broken Links seams.
  • The canonical identity is tag_id. Aliases are discovery inputs only and always resolve to a selected canonical Tag.
  • Group and current association titles are distinguishing lookup context; they are not copied into source identity.

Associations Are The Target

  • A Tag target is its complete ordered doc_url[] association set. There is no separate Tag landing page and no privileged primary document.
  • doc_url[0] occupies the first position in display order; it is not a unique canonical destination and not evidence of document ownership.
  • The Tag Registry remains authoritative for canonical Tag identity, group, aliases, and association order. Semantic Tokens consume a focused generated target projection and do not inspect or mutate canonical Tag JSON directly.
  • Document-location projection supplies current public-safe titles and URLs. A token never infers an association from document title, content, current route, report host, or neighbouring source.
  • The complete association set remains available to Manage target and usage data even when the rendered inline group has a smaller display limit.

Source And Authoring Alternatives

TST-1.0 must choose between two deliberate source contracts. Both produce the same visible result and preserve immutable canonical Tag identity.

Option A — Wrapped Selection

The action replaces the captured selection with a token containing the occurrence text:

[[tag:tag:nerve|nerve]]

The builder renders:

nerve ([Nerve], [Neural pathways])

This option fits the current three-part Semantic Token grammar. The token owns both the visible occurrence text and Tag identity; its Info view can edit the occurrence text while keeping identity readonly.

Option B — Postfix Token

The action leaves the selected prose in place and inserts a Tag marker after it:

nerve [[tag:tag:nerve]]

The postfix token renders only the parenthesised association group:

nerve ([Nerve], [Neural pathways])

This option matches the literal authoring model that the association group follows existing prose rather than replacing it. It requires a reviewed family-specific occurrence contract because the current grammar requires a Title field. TST-1 must not infer, rewrite, or repair the prose before a postfix token after ordinary source edits. Authored proximity is accepted as written; the author remains responsible for keeping it intelligible.

TST-1.0 must freeze the exact postfix syntax, whitespace ownership, punctuation behaviour, empty-selection behaviour, caret activation range, Info-view fields, and source-removal result. It must compare these costs with the wrapped form before selecting either option.

Association Rendering

  • The rendered suffix is one space followed by a parenthesised, comma-delimited sequence of ordinary document anchors.
  • Link labels use resolved document titles, not Tag IDs, array indexes, source filenames, or copied occurrence text.
  • Links follow exact doc_url[] order. They are never alphabetized or ranked during target generation or rendering.
  • The provisional inline display limit is three links. TST-1.0 must freeze the exact limit and the explicit overflow treatment; truncation must never be silent.
  • An over-limit occurrence should retain the complete ordered association set in Manage data and expose the omitted count in rendered or report state. The freeze decides whether excess links are represented by a non-link count, accessible disclosure, or an unavailable/over-limit result.
  • The zero-association, all-stale, and partially unavailable cases require explicit fixtures. The implementation must not silently select a different association, reorder the set, fabricate a landing page, or imply that a partial set is complete.
  • Public output is resolved at build time. Public readers receive ordinary anchors and no registry, lookup, usage index, or resolution runtime.

Tag Registry Ordering

Association order becomes user-visible whenever a Tag token is rendered, especially when a display limit applies. TST-1 therefore includes an explicit way to change doc_url[] order in Edit Tag.

  • Reordering edits the complete local association draft and is committed by the existing atomic Tag mutation boundary.
  • The UI must expose deliberate accessible ordering controls. TST-1.0 decides between move-up/move-down controls and another equally explicit interaction; drag-only ordering is insufficient.
  • Removing, adding, and reordering remain independent draft operations until Save. Close discards all of them.
  • No automatic title sort, availability sort, recently-used ranking, or semantic-token usage may rewrite canonical order.
  • Ordering conveys presentation priority only. It does not transfer document lifecycle ownership to Tag Registry or synchronize a document with Tag identity.
  • TST-1.0 must decide whether the display limit is presentation-only or whether Tag Registry should also enforce an association-count limit. The starting assumption is a presentation limit because canonical associations may have non-token consumers.

Target And Usage Projection

The current Semantic Tokens target row assumes one workable href. TST-1 must extend that contract deliberately rather than placing one Tag URL into the Catalogue shape.

A proposed Tag target row contains:

{
  "family": "tag",
  "target_type": "tag",
  "target_id": "nerve",
  "title": "nerve",
  "meta": ["subject"],
  "associations": [
    {"title": "Nerve", "href": "/analysis/?doc=...&subdoc=..."},
    {"title": "Neural pathways", "href": "/analysis/?doc=...&subdoc=..."}
  ]
}

The exact field names and unavailable-record representation remain a TST-1.0 freeze decision. Required semantics are:

  • one lookup row per canonical Tag;
  • ordered associations resolved from the exact stored URLs;
  • canonical aliases available to discovery without becoming target identity;
  • one usage occurrence per authored Tag token, not one fabricated token per linked document;
  • enough usage data to distinguish the complete target set, rendered subset, display limit, and overflow count; and
  • exact source document and source range for report navigation and targeted build preservation.

The Semantic Tokens report must find where the Tag token occurs without duplicating the occurrence merely because the Tag has several associations. Docs Broken Links remains the read-only diagnosis owner for unknown Tags and the association failure states frozen in TST-1.0.

Delivery Discipline

TST-1 is one complete second-family vertical slice. It should extend the proven generic Semantic Tokens seams only where Tag's one-to-many target genuinely requires it. It must not turn the registry into executable plugins, combine Tag and Catalogue search, add a generic graph, create a public Tag application, or move Tag Registry authority into Docs Viewer.

TST-1.0 must record the exact proposed files, reused seams, and rough production/test diff per later checkpoint. Any proposed generic multi-target framework must remain no larger than the Tag consumer needs and stop for review before implementation.

Likely Authority To Inspect

This is a routing map for TST-1.0, not a frozen file-change list.

boundary likely current owners delivery pressure
family definition and browser registry docs-viewer/config/semantic-tokens/registry.json and source-editor/semantic-token-registry.js register Tag without adding it to Catalogue discovery
canonical Tag identity and associations studio/data/canonical/tags/ and studio/services/tags/ project canonical IDs, aliases, groups, and ordered URLs without transferring authority
document association editing studio/app/frontend/js/tag-registry-* add accessible draft reordering while preserving complete-array atomic Save
target lookup docs_builder/semantic_target_lookup.py and Semantic Token target adapters add an ordered multi-document Tag projection without fabricating one primary href
source authoring and Info generic Source contribution/range seams plus new Tag-owned modules beside catalogue-token-* implement the selected wrapped or postfix contract and keep identity readonly
build and usage docs_builder/semantic_tokens.py and semantic_token_artifacts.py render the bounded parenthesised group and preserve one occurrence with complete association context

Delivery Steps

TST-1.0 — Trace And Freeze The Tag Family

  • [ ] Trace current Tag Registry ordering, aliases, document-location resolution, Semantic Token grammar, target lookup, Source contributions, builder projection, usage preservation, report, Broken Links, and public isolation.
  • [ ] Compare wrapped-selection and postfix-token fixtures, including source insertion, whitespace, punctuation, manual edits, Info activation/update, removal, save, rebuild, and public output.
  • [ ] Freeze canonical Tag identity, alias discovery, complete association-set semantics, ordered lookup shape, zero/stale/partial failure behaviour, and the rule for resolved usage.
  • [ ] Freeze the inline display limit, over-limit presentation, exact link labels, and whether the limit constrains only rendering or also canonical association count.
  • [ ] Freeze Edit Tag reordering interaction and complete-draft Save behaviour.
  • [ ] Record the exact files, reused seams, rough production/test diff, and any generic-contract expansion before implementation approval.

Checkpoint: reviewed fixtures cover wrapped and postfix source, collapsed and non-empty selections, punctuation, one/two/three/over-limit associations, reordered links, zero associations, stale first/middle/last associations, duplicate visible titles, alias discovery, targeted rebuild, usage rows, and public output. Stop before implementation.

TST-1.1 — Tag Lookup And Multi-Target Projection

  • [ ] Add the focused Tag target generator over canonical Registry, aliases, and public-safe document-location projections.
  • [ ] Extend the target schema and shared consumers only as required for one ordered association set.
  • [ ] Register the Tag family and implement tolerant build rendering for the chosen source contract, display limit, and frozen failure states.
  • [ ] Generate one usage occurrence with complete and rendered association evidence while preserving untouched documents during targeted builds.
  • [ ] Keep Tag canonical data, aliases, target lookup, and usage data out of public output.

Checkpoint: focused lookup, parser, builder, usage, targeted-build, and public-isolation evidence passes for the frozen fixtures. Stop for approval before TST-1.2.

TST-1.2 — Authoring, Info, And Association Ordering

  • [ ] Add the separate Add tag token Source action and Tag discovery modal with canonical ID, alias, group, and association context.
  • [ ] Insert the frozen wrapped or postfix source form through captured, revision-guarded Source mutation only.
  • [ ] Add the family-specific Info view with immutable identity, current target context, permitted occurrence editing, and exact-range removal.
  • [ ] Add accessible association reordering to the Edit Tag draft without changing its atomic complete-array mutation boundary.
  • [ ] Preserve validation, unavailable-target, and stale-range errors without adding redundant successful-mutation status messages.

Checkpoint: focused module and route evidence passes, and manual acceptance adds a Tag token from selected prose, reorders two associated documents, saves, rebuilds, and observes the same new order in the parenthesised links. Stop for approval before TST-1.3.

TST-1.3 — Reports, Regression, And Transfer

  • [ ] Extend the Semantic Tokens report and Docs Broken Links diagnosis for the frozen Tag occurrence and association states.
  • [ ] Prove Catalogue Work, Series, and Moment insertion, Info, rendering, usage, and unresolved behaviour are unchanged.
  • [ ] Verify one/two/three/over-limit associations, ordering, aliases, zero/stale/partial data, source edits, targeted rebuild preservation, public links, and public isolation.
  • [ ] Run focused Python, browser-module, lint, whitespace, generated docs, and search checks, then perform the mandatory final diff and omission review.
  • [ ] Transfer shipped behaviour to the concise Semantic Tokens, Tag Registry, Source Editor UI, Architecture, Target Lookup, and Usage Index owners.

Not In Scope

  • combining Tag targets with Catalogue discovery or the Catalogue toolbar action;
  • a unique primary Tag document or inferred doc_url[0] ownership;
  • automatic Tag-document creation, repair, deletion, or synchronization;
  • deriving associations from document titles, content, source proximity, or usage rows;
  • recursive relationship resolution or Resolver Token behaviour;
  • a public Tag registry, target lookup, usage index, or client-side resolver;
  • automatic repair of confusing postfix placement after manual source edits; or
  • changing document lifecycle because a URL is added, removed, or reordered.
